decisions.reason: Applying the bullet visual design across all templates does not change Tab-driven sublevel creation, hierarchy, or alignment behavior.
The style catalog already applies across the complete template set, and the source only broadens the scope of the separate bullet visual design requirement.
The scope of bullet-list visual design does not affect the templates' default document language or its unresolved English-versus-Danish conflict.
Requiring consistent bullet visuals across templates does not necessarily change legacy-content paste stability, test files, or Word-limitation constraints.
The source decision concerns bullet-list visual design and does not alter pasted-table structure or column containment.
The source decision does not change the required behavior of manual line breaks after pasted content.
Applying bullet visuals across all templates does not alter the NXQ style prefix, its application condition, or the language of style names.
The source broadens a specific bullet-design scope but does not change the supported Word environment or general reliability requirements.
